chunks: That was narrated by Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When a man swears three oaths in one sitting as a single oath while he is in the state of Ihram, he has incurred the penalty of breaking the oath; the blood-price (diyah) is to be shed (a camel or equivalent), and he must give it in charity."

key_terms.حَدُّ الْجِدَالِ: The penalty for breaking an oath
key_terms.مَحْرِمٌ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that swearing three oaths while in the state of Ihram constitutes a single act of 'disputation' (jidal), incurring a specific blood-price (diyah) rather than multiple penalties. This ruling highlights the unique legal status of Ihram, where specific transgressions trigger distinct compensatory measures, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the sanctity of the pilgrimage state. The requirement to give the diyah as charity underscores the spiritual purification aspect of expiating this specific breach of ritual integrity.
